heading: Toxic Box Office Collection Day 4 Highlight
paragraphs: Toxic Box Office Collection Updates: Yash’s Toxic: A Fairy Tale for Grown-Ups continues its run at the box office, though the film has seen its collections drop significantly after its record-breaking opening. On Day 4, the Geetu Mohandas directorial collected Rs 24.50 crore net in India across 17,612 shows, according to trade tracker Sacnilk.

With the Day 4 earnings, Toxic’s total India gross collection has reached Rs 227.50 crore, while its India net collection stands at Rs 190.45 crore. Its worldwide collection currently stands at Rs 254.75 crore.
The Kannada version of Toxic recorded an overall occupancy of 47.23% on Day 4. Meanwhile, the film’s Hindi version recorded an overall occupancy of 26.19%.
Toxic released on August 26 with a record-breaking Rs 101.10 crore net collection in India. However, the film witnessed a significant drop in collections over the following days.

The film has received a mixed response from audiences and critics. While some viewers have praised Yash’s screen presence, the film’s visuals and action sequences, others have criticised its writing, pacing and length. The divided response has sparked considerable discussion around the film since its release.

Amid the mixed reviews and divided audience response, Kantara director Rishab Shetty came out in support of Toxic. In a post on X, he praised Yash’s performance and the film’s attempt to take an unconventional route.

“As an artist, when you play a character, you try to bring it to life from the bottom of your heart. And here, I am truly impressed by the conviction with which the struggle of a powerful man has been portrayed. Maybe the plot and driving characters are not on the usual track on which most films travel, but that doesn’t mean the track is wrong. The effort that goes into telling a story, and the journey it takes from being a thought in the mind to becoming a film on screen, is humongous.”

Praising Yash, Rishab added, “Hats off to the way you have surrendered yourself to a character and a world that demands a larger-than-life performance. I could clearly feel that in every single scene. It’s not easy to give the audience an experience of how guilt multiplies and increases the toxicity in life. I stand with you for attempting this daring experiment, sir.”
He also praised Yash for his efforts to take Kannada cinema to the global stage and wished director Geetu Mohandas and the team at KVN Productions well.
Apart from Yash, Toxic also features Kiara Advani, Nayanthara, Tara Sutaria, Rukmini Vasanth, Huma Qureshi and Akshay Oberoi.
According to trade tracker Sacnilk, Toxic, currently running across 16,220 shows, has collected Rs 23 crore net as of 10 pm on Sunday.

X user @luvashwin wrote on X, "#toxic -ve reviews are real. Its high on style, zero in substance. Individual performance is good, visually its great, but no story. The so called climax sequences is good if viewed in isolation, but it don't sync with the movie. At best, avoid."
According to trade tracker Sacnilk, Toxic, currently running across 15,436 shows, has collected Rs 19.93 crore net as of 9 pm on Sunday.

User @emohanx said via X, "PR can sell tickets. It cannot shorten 3 hours.Watched #toxic in Tamil. @Toxic_themovie looks rich on screen. The camera work by Rajeev Ravi is the one thing that never drops: Goa, smoke, blood, faces, all framed like someone actually cared. Then the cracks show. Fights move so fast you lose the people inside them. When you cannot track who is hitting whom and why, the mass scenes go cold. @TheNameIsYash’s Raya is not a winner. He is shut off, rotting from the inside, still walking into the next fight the only way he knows. That choice works. Not every hero has to conquer. A decaying man with grit is rare. The romance does not. Scenes with @advani_kiara and the others keep coming, but there is little real warmth. After a while they feel like padding, not love. @GeetuMohandas made a film that is not bad. It is long. Second watch might give aftertaste. First watch already asks for patience most people will not give twice. Tamil dubbing is a disaster. Voices sit wrong on the faces. Dialogue needs to improved. Same care that went into Hindi should have gone here. Tamil audience paid the same ticket. Effort is huge. Shape is not."
According to trade tracker Sacnilk, Toxic, currently running across 13,946 shows, has collected Rs 18.37 crore net as of 8 pm on Sunday.

User @jammypants4 took to X to post, "Unpopular opinion:- (MAY CONTAIN TOXIC SPOILERS) #toxic should have released in two parts. Part 1:-Ganga & Raya’s integration into the Goa syndicate during Portuguese rule & flashbacks to their origin story. Nadia & Raya’s relationship & Elizabeth’s revenge! Climax: The reveal that Raya actually saved his son! Part 2:-Raya’s rise in Macau & the Portuguese leave India. Raya’s return to Goa, Ticket’s havoc that consumes him & an ultimate War between the gangs of Goa & Macau. Climax: Did Raya actually save his son & the REVEAL!"
User @movie__maniac shared on X, "More than #toxicthemovie itself, the audience reactions after the movie ends are more entertaining and funny. Every time I see these videos, they make me laugh."
According to trade tracker Sacnilk, Toxic, currently running across 12,508 shows, has collected Rs 16.79 crore net as of 7 pm on Sunday.

User @FilmiHindustani's note on X read, "Years later.. as Raya heads towards the hospital because he is going to be a father, he gets surrounded by a group of goons. He takes down most of them, but one escapes.. a teenager. During the entire fight, Raya’s body gets covered in blood. And in that exact state..drenched in blood, he holds his newborn son Adam in his arms for the very first time in his life. What follows is one of the most brilliantly layered scenes in the film.. and one that many completely missed. Raya looks at newborn Adam (Actually the second son), but suddenly starts seeing his first son in front of him. And there’s a reason for that. The teenager who escaped is roughly the same age his first son would have been after all these years. This entire sequence marks the beginning of GUILT taking over Raya’s mind.. a guilt that had been buried deep inside him all these years. The blood covering Raya becomes a metaphor for the blood of his first son.. the guilt of having killed his own child. And with that guilt literally covering his body, he picks up his newborn son. And ironically.. when Raya was born, he was splattered with his own father’s blood. That scene beautifully trace Raya’s journey from a child born into violence to a father haunted by the violence he himself has committed. That’s when the hallucination of his first son begins. It’s not just a hallucination. It’s guilt, trauma, memory and fatherhood colliding in a single frame. This is not just a 'confusing' scene. It’s a deeply psychological visual representation of guilt consuming a man from within. Peak detailing by Geetu Mohandas. #toxic."

User @itschinna18 tweete, "Walked out of d theatre. no matter how bad a film is, i never do this shit. loved d entire first half. acting, direction, screenplay, cinematography everything was top notch. and then d torture started in second half. i left the theatre with more than 45 minutes still left.#toxic. from the beginning of the second half, everything went off track immediately. but the moment small Yash (Ticket) came on screen, i just couldn’t bear it anymore and walked out. Ravi Basrur should take a small break man. small Yash and Ravi’s BGM combo was so torturous"

According to trade tracker Sacnilk, Toxic, currently running across 9,560 shows, has collected Rs 10.86 crore net as of 4 pm on Sunday.

Reddit user @Infamous-Ad4993 shared his Toxic review that read, "I loved this movie and could definitely give 7/10 rating, I watched with open mind and has 0 expectations after all negative comments, however its not a bad movie though, guys u should definitely watch it and try to understand concept."

Trade analyst Rohit Jaiswal shared via X, "Toxic hasn’t quite reached the business level that I expected from the film. There’s no point denying that the numbers so far are considerably below expectations, and perhaps it’s best to let the audience’s verdict speak for itself with grace…… BUT…. There is one silver lining it’s TOXIC Day 1 collection, power and superstardom of Yash in Hindi Heartland…… The reviews were already out by morning, and the audience knew what the word-of-mouth was. Yet, the opening remained strong. That says something significant, the love, respect and trust that audiences have for Yash is very much intact or else collection would have fallen from 2pm….. Day 1 reflects the star pull. From Day 2 onwards, the audience decides the journey which has been already declared…… And I genuinely believe the audience will give Yash another opportunity. With #ramayana Part 1 and Part 2 coming in next fourteen months, there is plenty to look forward to. If #ramayan connects with the audience the way I hope it does, #toxic will eventually become just another chapter in YASH much bigger journey. It’s time for @TheNameIsYash to move from Toxic to Ramayan, and announce a new fresh massy pan India film for 2028……"

X page @MovieReview_Hub shared, "My last thought on #toxic: I genuinely feel that if #toxic had been made with a smaller actor on a modest budget, it could have turned into a typical Malayali psychological thriller and possibly even a blockbuster. But Geethu Mohandas and #yash couldn’t quite handle the pressure of presenting a superstar on the big screen in a larger-than-life role after the success of #kgf2. That pressure seems to have taken away a lot from the story, which was actually very strong on paper. The focus gradually shifted from storytelling to Aura Farming, and that, for me, is where #toxic lost its potential. In attempt to make Yash bigger star than other, they took unnecessary from other movies from action scenes to bold scenes to being N*ked and lost entire purpose of story."

Siddharth R Kannan said via X, "The more you hear about #toxic, the more insane this film starts sounding. #yash in a completely different avatar, a world that looks larger than life and that mass factor we’ve been waiting for. Is #toxic the next big game-changer for Indian cinema? Your expectations HUGE or MASSIVE?"

According to trade tracker Sacnilk, Toxic, currently running across 7,291 shows, has collected Rs 4.25 crore net as of 1 pm on Sunday. This brings the film's total India gross collections to Rs 233.26 crore and total India net collection to Rs 195.35 crore.

User @bekoopa's post on Reddit read, "Watched the movie Toxic today (Kannada). Me and my wife. We went with no expectations and surprisingly both of us totally enjoyed the movie! Not sure why so much negative publicity about this. Some of the scenes felt slow a bit in the first half. But it picked up the pace really well. Yash’s acting is amazing. Trailer already shows double role. So hope this is not a spoiler. The younger role of Yash has been made really well and he has acted really good.The plot twist and climax are so well made. Feeling bad that so many negative reviews and spoilers are out to destroy the movie’s box office run. Definitely recommended people to watch it."

According to trade tracker Sacnilk, Toxic, currently running across 5,533 shows, has collected Rs 2.79 crore net as of 12 pm on Sunday. This brings the film's total India gross collections to Rs 231.54 crore and total India net collection to Rs 193.89 crore.

Reddit user @Dry_Pea_2328 posted, "I honestly can’t believe how some people are saying they couldn’t understand Toxic. What exactly was so complicated? The story and its underlying message were pretty straightforward if you paid attention. The concept is bold, unconventional and far more layered than the usual predictable commercial film. It doesn’t spoon-feed every emotion or explain every scene through unnecessary dialogue it trusts the audience to observe, connect the details and understand the characters’ motivations. Geetu Mohandas has created a distinctive world with atmosphere, style and substance, while Yash has delivered a powerful and controlled performance. His screen presence is exceptional, but the film also gives him more than just mass moments. There is intensity, vulnerability and purpose behind the character. Of course, everyone is entitled to their opinion, but the coordinated negativity surrounding this movie feels excessive. Some people appear determined to dismiss it without even engaging with what the film is trying to do. Something is seriously wrong when audiences demand fresh concepts and then immediately attack a filmmaker for attempting something different. For me, Toxic is daring, visually striking and conceptually strong. Geetu and Yash have delivered. Perhaps this is one of those films that people will understand and appreciate more with time."

X user @seeuatthemovie shared, "Everyone is so quick to blame Geetu Mohandas for the debacle that Toxic is, but it’s so evident that the garbage dialogue, pointless action & sexist female character treatment masquerading as 'MASSY' are all #yash’s so called 'creative' vision. He obviously Ghost Directed it."

X user @RichieCreation1 shared, "A slow poison. #toxic The more I think about it, the deeper it gets—life, choices, guilt, loss & the sacrifices we make for what we think we need. Watched it once, yet every scene reveals something new. Thank you @TheNameIsYash sir for an experience, not another baseless film."

According to trade tracker Sacnilk, Toxic, currently running across 4,810 shows, has collected Rs 1.70 crore net as of 11 am on Sunday. This brings total India gross collections to Rs 229.51 crore and total India net collection to Rs 192.15 crore.

User @Toxic_Sarfu tweeted, "Will never forgive #yash & Geetu for Not preparing us and Not calling #toxicthemovie a psychological thriller beforehand Felt average on the First watch, but after 3 watches..... Everything is just PERFECT Never seen anything like this before! For me, Toxic > KGF!!"

Trade analyst Vishwajit Patil criticised Yash over his recent appearance on Aap Ki Adalat. Reacting to the actor’s comment that he is “not a superstar again,” he wrote, "The sheer arrogance of #yash on Aap Ki Adalat! Claiming he's 'not superstar again' because he thinks he's already the ultimate No. 1 in India? One franchise doesn't make you the king of Indian Cinema. Pure delusion on display. #toxicthemovie #toxic."

Prominent North Indian exhibitor Manoj Desai has praised Toxic for its box office performance, claiming that the film is doing “really excellent” business in his theatres. According to Desai, on Day 4, around 80% of the shows at his theatres were housefull. His comments come amid discussions around the film’s box office performance.

X user MNV Gowda praised Kannada stars Kichcha Sudeepa and Upendra for extending their support to Yash and Toxic, especially when the film is facing mixed reactions. The user posted on X,"The maturity and support shown by @KicchaSudeep sir and @nimmaupendra sir, especially when things aren’t going #toxicthemovie’s way, shows the respect and solidarity they have for their fellow artists, immense respect from my side as always . Their Gesture is a beautiful reminder that #sandalwood is more than an industry it is a family."

Trade analyst Parth Chaturvedi too to X to post "#toxicthemovie is doing well at single screens and in mass circuits. Had a word with one exhibitor running a single screen with over 450 capacity, and as per him, occupancy is clocking over 80% in his cinema. So it feels like… the movie is getting acceptance in mass circuits. Although, in era of multiplex, sustainable collection requires constant business in multiplexes. As of now net collection stands at Rs 190.45 Crore for initial 4 days. Hindi is still continuing to put more money in collections, but there is substantial decline in Hindi as well on Saturday with Rs 16 Crore collection approx."

On Day 4, Toxic recorded its highest collection from the Hindi version, which earned Rs 15.50 crore at 23.0% occupancy across 12,822 shows. The Kannada version followed with Rs 6.60 crore at 47.0% occupancy across 1,341 shows. The Telugu version collected Rs 1.50 crore with 23.0% occupancy from 1,672 shows, while the Tamil version earned Rs 0.75 crore at 17.0% occupancy across 1,500 shows. The Malayalam version contributed Rs 0.15 crore at 21.0% occupancy across 277 shows.
Toxic witnessed a 9.9% drop in its India net collection on Day 4, earning Rs 24.50 crore compared to Rs 27.20 crore on Day 3.

In the overseas market, Toxic collected Rs 4 crore on Day 4, taking its total overseas gross collection to Rs 27.25 crore. With this, the Yash-starrer has pushed its worldwide gross collection to Rs 254.75 crore.

According to trade tracker Sacnilk, on Day 4, Toxic collected Rs 24.50 crore net across 17,612 shows in India. With this, the Yash-starrer has taken its total India gross collections to Rs 227.50 crore, while its total India net collection stands at Rs 190.45 crore.
